newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended a see-saw session virtually unchanged, supported by a stronger peseta amid lacklustre trading.
"In the short run the worst could be over," a dealer said.
He added that with January inflation data ahead, the Iberian market could rebound a bit.
But analysts added there was a change in sentiment and they expect the bonos would not move a lot from the actual levels.
The 10-year spread over Bunds ended the session at around 105 basis points, little changed from yesterday's 106 bps but well off Friday's 92 bps.
The yield curve recovered a bit after having flattened for a week, with the spread between the two- and 10-year benchmark at around 124 basis points from 122 bps this morning.
Treasury will offer tomorrow five-, 15-year bonds, and one-year bills. Dealers expect yields on the latter to pick up from the previous auction to around 5.15 percent from 5.052 pct.
